newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ share prices end softly on high turnover.
newsitem.headline: NZ share prices end softly on high turnover.

text.p: * New Zealand share prices ended on a soft note
* Market largely withstands effect of sharp falls offshore
* Turnover high. Ceramco claws back ground
New Zealand share prices largely withstood sharp falls in overseas markets to end Friday's session just slightly down.
The NZSE-40 Capital Index ended 12.60 points (0.53 percent) down at 2,349.91 on turnover worth NZ$70.6 million.

Australia's All Ords was down 36 points (1.56 percent) at 2,307.80 and Japan's Nikkei Index was off by more than 500 points (2.5 percent) at 19,987, both in response to Wall Street's 100-point decline.
"It wasn't a bad performance when you look at the other markets," Don Turkington at Cavill White Securities said.
There was good two-way business in Fletcher Building, which was level at NZ$4.25, and Telecom, which eased two cents to NZ$7.35.
"There were a number of stocks that performed pretty well given the market conditions," Turkington.
But Brierley Investments, down two at NZ$1.28, Fletcher Energy, down five at NZ$3.95, and Carter Holt Harvey, off six at $3.32, all succumbed to selling pressure.
"It was a mixed picture, but really we are only down 12 points and I think that is a pretty creditable performance," he said.
Whether the market continued to hold would be largely dependent whether the foreign markets stemmed their losses.
"It will find it difficult to go up, so we are a little at the mercy of the larger markets," he said.
Ceramics and lingerie maker Ceramco, out of favour for many months, showed signs of a clawback by gaining eight to NZ$1.28.
There was good volume in DB Group, itself a reflection of differing views on what an appropriate level for the stock is after its announced capital reconstruction.
